      "definition": "F6 is the source's family for claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance, covering EVALUATION §§1–5.       "label":"Claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"A load-bearing claim identifies an exact subject, claimed property, governing basis, witness-to-claim relation, nearest excluded weaker property and falsifier. Its boundary, quantifier, population and scope determine what evidence can support it.",

      "label":"Load-bearing claim"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"The semantic basis comprises constitutional and accepted-design relations defining claim meaning; the evidence basis comprises exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations; the state projection is a current view derived from admitted semantic and evidence bases.       "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":140,"quote":"Three bases stay distinct (P6, P1): the semantic basis, the constitutional\nand accepted-design relations that define what a claim means; the evidence\nbasis, the exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations used to\nevaluate it; and the state projection, a current view derived from admitted\nsemantic and evidence bases.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F2.%20Separation","start_line":134}],

      "label":"Evaluation bases and roles"

      "label":"Structural conformance and semantic fidelity"
    },

      "definition":"Independent assessment evaluates the exact live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state. It is distinct from construction and constructor self-review. Independence rests on authorship and evidence conditions, not context freshness.",

      "key":"independent_assessment",
      "label":"Independent assessment"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"Author identity is the party responsible for a realised subject's content. Actor identity identifies whoever performs an operation and is not itself authority. Assessment independence is judged against authorship as well as evidence conditions.",

    },

      "label":"Review result"

    {

      "label":"Core review result domain"

      "conditions": [],

      "grounding":[{"end_line":321,"quote":"Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject;\nrecording it cannot widen it, and it exhausts only the instance and interval\nit names","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F5.%20Acceptance","start_line":312}],
      "key":"acceptance_and_closure",
      "label":"Acceptance and closure"

      "definition":"The successor disposition record identifies the exact predecessor immutable cut and one semantic disposition for every predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor. It forms part of successor acceptance evidence.",

      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":346,"quote":"A finding is a defect a review reports against the exact claim it\nevaluated (§4).       "key":"promotion_blocking",
      "label":"Finding and promotion blocking"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"A realisation aⱼ conforms to specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract and independent judgment. Semantic conformance uses the governing semantic basis as Σ.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":393,"quote":"A realisation aⱼ conforms to a specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour\nsatisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract (P1) and an independent\njudgment (P6).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F6.%20Conformance%20of%20realisations","start_line":388}],
      "key":"realisation_conformance",
      "label":"Conformance of realisations"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"The equivalence ladder is an unordered list of four separate claims: conformance; semantic equivalence, meaning identical interpreted behaviour between two realisations or a realisation and declared reference outcome on a stated domain, including behaviour outside Σ; computational equivalence, meaning the same function at equal cost on declared workloads and architecture H; and categorical equivalence of categories and maps. Preservation of identities and composition is an additional separate map claim. Semantic equivalence here is not cross-context conceptual equivalence.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":415,"quote":"The ladder is the list of the four claims named next,\neach a rung; the rungs are listed, not ordered, and no rung implies\nanother.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F6.%20Conformance%20of%20realisations","start_line":395}],
      "key":"equivalence_ladder",
      "label":"Equivalence ladder"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"A layered specification is sufficient when a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from each layer.       "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":443,"quote":"A specification arranged in layers is sufficient when\na competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from each layer; the\nderivation need not be unique","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F6.%20Conformance%20of%20realisations","start_line":428}],
      "key":"layered_sufficiency",
      "label":"Layered sufficiency and reconstructability"
    },
    {
      "conditions":["A task builds or assesses one successor member against its predecessor."],
      "definition":"A reconstruction return separates three heads and their evidence: semantic conservation preserves a disposed predecessor claim's meaning, judged by reading both texts against the disposition; demonstrated reduction traces the same deciding path in both versions and shows lower successor cost under a declared measure and tradeoffs; mere relocation moves text between owners or carriers without meaning change or a traced deciding-path change.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":482,"quote":"A reconstruction return is the return of a task that builds or assesses\none member of a successor against its predecessor.       "key":"reconstruction_return",
      "label":"Reconstruction return"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"F7 covers EVALUATION §§6–7 and CONFORMANCE, addressing fitness claims about realisations, frames and the method.       "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":501,"quote":"Its instance premises are: (a)\none specification may have several realisations; (b) realisations, frames\nand the method are made by fallible constructors and relied on by actors\nwho did not make them; (c) qualification evidence comes from a finite set\nof cases, run by actors inside declared envelopes.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F6.%20Conformance%20of%20realisations%2FFoundation%20to%20law%3A%20conformance%2C%20equivalence%20and%20qualification","start_line":491}],

      "label":"Conformance, equivalence and qualification"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"EVALUATION §7 is the document container for qualification of frames and of the method. Its supplied heading alone adds no qualification procedure.",

Qualification of frames and of the method","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F7.%20Qualification%20of%20frames%20and%20of%20the%20method","start_line":545}],
      "key":"qualification_section",
      "label":"Qualification section"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"Frame qualification evaluates a candidate frame in proportion to its claims, with nine minimum tests: decision, reconstruction, sensitivity, irrelevance, basis, authority, counterexample, capability and result consumption.       "exceptions": [],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":578,"quote":"Qualification binds the exact frame revision, actor envelope, evaluation\nfamily, basis class and evidence conditions evaluated.       "key":"frame_qualification",
      "label":"Frame qualification"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"Fit asks whether the actor class can hold the frame; context fit compares measured selected-representation size with declared capacity.       "key":"fit_and_adequate_attention",

    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"Method self-qualification applies ordinary qualification, consuming the work boundary, construction-and-assessment relation and layered sufficiency without creating another process.       "grounding":[{"end_line":618,"quote":"The method is qualified the way it qualifies anything else.       "key":"method_self_qualification",
      "label":"Method self-qualification"

    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition":"The qualification population names declare, activate, evaluate, conjoin, translate, audit_coverage, revise, result consumption and material composition. These are represented operations with distinct observation obligations; this interpretation performs none of them.",

      "grounding":[{"end_line":644,"quote":"The qualification population is every function and failure relation the\nmethod claims (REFERENCE_FRAME §5), each with its required representative\nobservations (P6):","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation/claude/9aee01ffa76cfbde1a6b8f1153a25bd6d71c216e/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F7.%20Qualification%20of%20frames%20and%20of%20the%20method%2FMethod%20self-qualification","start_line":630}],
